subject: community-medicine
title: Family planning programme and related legislation

steps.tx: An **eligible couple** is a currently married couple in which the wife is in the reproductive age group, 15 to 49 years. Target couples are a narrower group, usually those with 2 to 3 living children, toward whom family planning was originally directed. Do not confuse the two terms in exams.
steps.say: An eligible couple is a currently married couple in which the wife is in the reproductive age group, fifteen to forty nine years. Target couples are a narrower group, usually those with two to three living children, toward whom family planning was originally directed. Do not confuse the two terms in exams.

steps.tx: The **couple protection rate** (CPR) is the percentage of eligible couples protected by an approved method, namely sterilisation, IUD, condom or oral pills. CPR is the key indicator of contraceptive prevalence. Worked example: 140 protected out of 200 eligible couples gives a CPR of 70 per cent. Effective CPR also weighs each method by its effectiveness.

steps.tx: A **net reproduction rate** (NRR) of 1 means each generation replaces itself, roughly equal to the two-child norm. NRR is achieved only when CPR exceeds 60 per cent, because about half to 60 per cent of births are third or higher order. Sterilisation accounts for over 60 per cent of protected couples in the programme.

steps.tx: The **National Population Policy 2000** set a medium-term goal of bringing the **total fertility rate** to replacement level, 2.1, by 2010. Its long-term objective is a stable population by 2045. Other goals include a maternal mortality ratio below 100 per 100000 live births and infant mortality below 30 per 1000 live births. Note that the goal of 2015 is not in the policy.
